title: Anchored Audit Evidence Export Playbook and WORM Anchoring for Admin Access Events
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Purpose: Define and deliver an export playbook and storage anchoring for admin-facing audit evidence (admin actions, access attempts, configuration changes) that satisfies WORM integrity, residency controls, and automated reporting for legal/compliance requests. This ticket designs the canonical export format, the retention/lock lifecycle, and verification tooling used by the Console and Private control plane. Scope excludes user-level application logs and operational metrics; focuses on admin-level audit trails and export/evidence bundles required for legal holds and cross-region escrow.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical export format defined and documented (JSONL manifest + detached Merkle index) and approved by security
Daily and ad-hoc evidence bundles can be produced via API and Console export with strong integrity proofs (signed Merkle root + object lock), with residency tag applied
Exported bundles are stored with enforced retention/lock (Cloud Object Lock or on-prem equivalent) and verified via automated verifier that checks signatures, hashes, and retention metadata
Playbook includes steps for customer-provided escrow handoff and for internal SOC/Legal requests, with clear audit trail of the export operation
End-to-end integration test demonstrates creation -> WORM-locking -> verification -> tamper-detection, and relevant dashboards show export metrics and failures
technical_design: Overview: We will produce evidence bundles containing a compressed set of audit events (admin actions, access auth events, config diffs) partitioned by region/residency and day. Each bundle is serialized as newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with canonical field ordering and a deterministic signing canonicalization. A per-bundle Merkle tree will be computed over canonicalized event bytes; the Merkle root is signed with a hardware-backed signing key (HSM/KMS with signing-only role). The bundle and its Merkle index are stored as immutable objects in the region-specific storage namespace with object-lock retention set to 'COMPLIANCE' mode for the required retention window. The Merkle roots are published to an append-only ledger index (daily ledger file) which itself is WORM-anchored and cross-region replicated. For on-prem/private customers, a local object-store wrapper will support the same retention and provides an API to export a signed bundle and a verifier utility.
tasks: Design canonical JSONL schema and canonicalization rules and publish Confluence spec
Implement Merkle tree generator library (golang) with deterministic canonicalization and tests
Integrate signing step using KMS/HSM sign-only key; ensure key rotation policy documented
Add object-store write path that sets object-lock retention+legal-hold metadata and region residency tags
Expose /audit/v1/exports endpoint (POST) to create on-demand evidence bundles and status polling endpoint
Add Console export workflow (UI + backend) with guided legal-hold options and verification link
Build verifier CLI that checks bundle integrity: hashes, Merkle proofs, signature validation, and object-lock metadata
Create end-to-end test harness: generate synthetic admin events -> export -> lock -> verify -> tamper attempt simulation
Draft playbook steps for SOC/Legal including escrow handoff checklist and chain-of-custody record format
Add metrics and alerts: export success/fail rate, lock failure events, verification failures, time-to-export SLA
notes: Retention enforcement: use object-lock where available; for storage backends without object-lock, implement policy agent that prevents delete and records legal-hold via ledger records and access controls
Residency: export bundles must be tagged with residency metadata and optionally stored in region-only vaults. Cross-region escrow copies must be explicit and recorded in ledger with customer consent
Privacy: redact PII in exported admin traces where not required by request; provide config toggle for full vs. redacted exports and record who requested full exports
Performance: daily bundles expected to contain up to 50M events for enterprise customers; streaming Merkle computation and chunked uploads required to keep memory bounded
Interoperability: make manifest consumable by third-party e-discovery tools; include schema versioning and human-readable index file
